page0.text:
We climb over the "NO TRESPASSING" fence and enter the temple yard.
Since our encounter with Caster, Ryudou Temple is now treated as important evidence in the mass coma case and closed to the public.

page1.text:
"..."
The air here still feels the same on my skin.
It's uncomfortably lukewarm, with the smell of ripe fruit.

page2.text:
"...We're going in, Saber."
"Yes. Be careful, Shirou."
"I know. Tell me right away if you sense danger."

page3.text:
...We pass through the yard and ascend a corridor leading to the inner temple.
The hallway is dark, and the wooden floor creaks with our every step.

page4.text:
"...Nothing feels especially off to me. How about you, Saber?"
"...I feel the same. But I am sure that something is strange about this entire area. Since we stepped foot atop this mountain, we have entered a space governed by a different set of rules.
In fact, I would say that our failure to notice anything amiss despite the abnormal amount of mana in the air is itself strange."

page5.text: "...Yeah. Okay, let's see what else we can dig up. There's a pond in the back of the temple, plus several buildings."

page6.text:
It's said that the pond was once home to a dragon.
We might be able to find some clues there, since it's long been considered a holy place.

page7.text:
We exit the corridor and head for the back of the temple.
Suddenly—
"Shirou!"

page8.text:
"Saber!?"
Something throws me from the corridor into the central shrine.
I realize that Saber did it, and I try to rush back to her side,
but Saber slams the door in my face.

page9.text:
"Saber!? What do you think you're doing...!?"
I pound on the door.
The door feels as hard as iron. Maybe Saber used some kind of spell on it.

page10.text:
"Damn it! What the hell! Open the door, Saber!"
I pound and punch the door, but it doesn't budge. It doesn't even give against a full-body tackle.

page11.text:
On the other side of the iron-hard door...
"Defend yourself, Shirou! This enemy is sure to target you!"

page12.text:
"W-what enemy!? The Shadow!?"
"No! It is the worst Servant a Master could hope to face! I'm sorry, but I cannot guarantee your safety on this battlefield.
That Servant—Assassin prefers to kill Masters first, rather than duel other Servants!"

page13.text:
"Assassin!?"
I didn't sense anything.
No matter how strange the air in Ryudou Temple feels, a Servant's aura is on a different level.
When a Servant materializes itself nearby, it gives off an unmistakably dense aura.
Even if it's hiding its aura, there's no way Saber would fail to sense it!

page14.text:
"I'm going to end this in a single strike. Please stay there!"
I feel Saber moving away.
Saber's footsteps are faint but firm. Maybe she's closing in on Assassin while fending off its attacks.

page15.text:
"Damn it. I'd better..."
I look around me.
I pick up a kyousaku stick that's handy enough to be a weapon, and immediately start Strengthening it.

page16.text:
"Hurry..."
I need to use it as a sword to cut the door open.
A bad hunch, an irritation I can't quite place starts to overtake my mind.
If I leave her here...
If I leave Saber alone on this mountain, there's no going back. I have to hurry up and—

page17.text:
"!?"
The lights go out.
No, there were never any lights here to begin with.
The moonlight that was illuminating the shrine is snuffed out.

page18.text:
"Ngh..."
Something reeks.
It's the odor of rotting meat, and the grating buzz of insect wings.

page19.text:
"Zouken Matou."
I stare into the darkness.
"Heh. Like a moth to the flame, young Emiya brat."
He cackles.
Somewhere out there, I feel the old mage's unmistakable, fiendish aura.

page20.text:
"Saber..."
I take a stance with my improvised weapon.
I'm not afraid of this centuries-old fiend.
The absent Saber's well-being is the only thing on my mind.
